metadata.name: Oʻahu Household-Item Disposal Finder V1 Data
metadata.scope: Residential household disposal guidance for 25 frozen canonical topics on Oʻahu.
metadata.authoritative_source_owner: City and County of Honolulu Department of Environmental Services (ENV)
metadata.disclaimer: Independent civic-tech pilot derived from public City guidance; not an official City service. Verify time-sensitive details with the authoritative source before disposal.

source_precedence: Use a current item-specific ENV page when it directly addresses the material.
Use current resident drop-off rules to refine preparation, quantity, and prohibited-item details.
Use current facility pages to determine location-specific acceptance and hours.
Use the general How to Dispose page as broader context/fallback.
When sources differ in specificity without an explicit contradiction, preserve all provenance and apply the more specific rule.
When sources materially conflict and cannot be reconciled, do not guess; mark the record unresolved and require ENV confirmation.

unsupported.message: This item/type is not covered by the frozen V1 corpus. Do not guess; use the authoritative ENV disposal guidance.

official_battery_source.message: The battery type cannot be resolved safely from the information provided. Check ENV's battery guidance or contact ENV.

official_paint_source.message: This paint type is outside the two frozen V1 paint topics. Use ENV's paint guidance.

official_how_to_dispose_source.message: This item is outside the frozen V1 topic set. Use ENV's How to Dispose guidance.

official_ewaste_source.message: This electronic item is outside the frozen V1 electronic topics. Use ENV's E-Waste Recycling guidance.

items.name: Large appliance

primary_pathway.next_action: Schedule bulky-item collection or take the household appliance to an eligible City disposal site.

restrictions: City resident rules limit large appliances to 2 per month.
Household types only; no commercial equipment.
Keʻehi Transfer Station does not accept large metal appliances.

alternatives.label: Dealer removal, donation, or qualifying refrigerator/freezer programs may be available.

items.name: Small appliance

primary_pathway.next_action: Dispose of the small appliance with regular household refuse; self-haul household refuse may also go to City convenience centers or transfer stations.

restrictions: If the appliance contains a non-removable/embedded battery, use the embedded-battery device guidance instead.
notes: Resident rules list microwaves, toasters and sewing machines as regular refuse examples.

primary_pathway.next_action: Schedule bulky-item collection or take the bicycle to a City disposal site and follow the site's metal-sorting instructions.

alternatives.label: Repair/donation or City-referenced recycling drives may be preferable for usable bicycles.

items.name: Computer / laptop

primary_pathway.next_action: For recycling, take the computer or laptop to a City e-waste bin at any listed convenience center or transfer station.

restrictions: If the disposal concern is a damaged/swollen battery that is removed or non-removable, use the battery clarification path rather than assuming the ordinary computer route.

alternatives.label: ENV also lists donation, manufacturer/retailer take-back, and local e-waste recycler options.

primary_pathway.next_action: For recycling, take the television or computer monitor to a City e-waste bin at any listed convenience center or transfer station.

alternatives.label: ENV also lists donation, manufacturer/retailer take-back, and local e-waste recycler options; fees may apply at some private recyclers.

items.name: Cell phone

primary_pathway.next_action: Use a service-provider, manufacturer, donation, or e-waste-recycler program referenced by ENV; confirm current acceptance with the provider.

restrictions: City e-waste drop-off bins explicitly list mobile telephones as unacceptable.
If the phone's non-removable battery is the disposal concern, use the embedded-battery device pathway.
notes: This topic intentionally does not route cell phones to City e-waste bins.

items.name: Embedded-battery electronic device

primary_pathway.next_action: Schedule the device for a City Household Hazardous Waste event, or use an ENV-listed e-waste recycler/free collection event that accepts embedded-battery devices.

preparation: Before contacting HHW, estimate the total device weight and identify the device/material for registration.
restrictions: HHW drop-off is by appointment and only registered items are accepted under current event rules.

alternatives.label: ENV says an e-waste recycler or free collection event may accept the entire device with its non-removable battery.

items.name: Standalone lithium / rechargeable battery

primary_pathway.next_action: Tape the terminals, place the standalone battery in a clear plastic bag, and take it to any City convenience center or transfer station.

preparation: Place the battery in a clear plastic bag.
restrictions: This rule is for standalone batteries. If the battery is still built into/non-removable from a device, use the embedded-battery pathway.
prohibitions: Do not dispose of standalone lithium/rechargeable batteries in regular trash.

items.name: Alkaline battery

primary_pathway.next_action: Dispose of regular household alkaline batteries with regular refuse.

restrictions: Do not use this rule for lithium/rechargeable, embedded, vehicle, heavy-equipment, or electric-vehicle batteries.

items.name: Vehicle lead-acid battery

primary_pathway.next_action: When purchasing a replacement, give the old car or motorcycle battery to the retailer; otherwise, residents may take eligible lead-acid car/motorcycle batteries to City convenience centers or transfer stations.

restrictions: City resident rule is for lead-acid car and motorcycle batteries only.
Heavy-equipment batteries and electric-vehicle batteries are not covered/accepted under this City drop-off rule.

items.name: Fire extinguisher

primary_pathway.next_action: Take an eligible residential fire extinguisher to a City convenience center, Kapaʻa Transfer Station, or Kawailoa Transfer Station.

restrictions: City resident rules list residential types A and B only; commercial types C, D, and E are not accepted.
Keʻehi Transfer Station does not accept fire extinguishers/compressed gas.

items.name: Furniture / mattress / carpet

primary_pathway.next_action: Schedule a bulky-item collection appointment or take the household item to a City disposal site.

preparation: Fasten rugs/carpeting when self-hauling, consistent with resident regular-refuse examples.

alternatives.label: Donate usable furniture or household items where accepted.

items.name: Household hazardous chemical

primary_pathway.next_action: Identify the exact chemical on ENV's Household Hazardous Waste guidance before disposing of it; materials routed to HHW must be registered for an appointment.

preparation: Keep the original label when possible.
Keep different HHW products separated; do not mix products.
For appointment registration, inventory the material type, container size, and quantity.
restrictions: Different household chemicals have different City disposal methods; this generic topic must not guess a method from the word 'chemical' alone.
Large quantities require contacting the Refuse Division for instructions.

items.name: Medication

primary_pathway.next_action: Use a medication drop-box/take-back program referenced by ENV and check the linked locator for current locations.

restrictions: Medication guidance is separate from sharps/needles and from prohibited medical waste at City disposal sites.

alternatives.label: ENV references Hawaiʻi overdose-prevention drop boxes and National Prescription Drug Take Back Day.

items.name: Oxygen tank

primary_pathway.next_action: Do not take an oxygen tank to a City convenience center or transfer station; contact an ENV-listed recycling company to confirm acceptance.

prohibitions: Oxygen tanks are listed as prohibited items at City resident disposal sites.

alternatives.label: ENV lists AirGas, Matheson, and Refrigerant Recycling as companies to contact; confirm current acceptance/fees directly.

items.name: Fluorescent tube / bulb

primary_pathway.next_action: Schedule an appointment for a City Household Hazardous Waste event, or confirm an ENV-referenced retailer take-back option.

restrictions: HHW drop-off is appointment-based and subject to current registration/event limits.

alternatives.label: ENV suggests checking retailers such as Home Depot for take-back.

items.name: Helium tank

primary_pathway.next_action: Take an eligible household helium tank to a City convenience center, Kapaʻa Transfer Station, or Kawailoa Transfer Station.

restrictions: City resident rules specify helium tanks of 14.9 cu. ft.
Keʻehi Transfer Station does not accept helium/compressed gas.
If the tank does not match the listed household size/type, contact ENV Disposal Branch instead of assuming acceptance.

items.name: Latex / oil paint

primary_pathway.next_action: Absorb the liquid paint with suitable absorbent material or air-dry it in the can; once contained/dry, place it in regular refuse.

preparation: Absorb liquid in a plastic bag with material such as shredded newspaper, old rags, or sawdust and seal the bag; or air-dry paint in the can.
restrictions: This topic covers latex/water-based and oil paint. Aerosol, lead, aluminum, paint thinner/stripper, and other hazardous paint products can require HHW handling.

items.name: Lead / aluminum paint

primary_pathway.next_action: Schedule the paint for a City Household Hazardous Waste event.

restrictions: HHW drop-off is by appointment and only registered items are accepted under current event rules.

items.name: Propane tank / cylinder

primary_pathway.next_action: Do not put the propane tank in trash. Take an eligible household propane tank/cylinder to a City convenience center, Kapaʻa Transfer Station, or Kawailoa Transfer Station.

restrictions: Keʻehi Transfer Station does not accept compressed gas.
City resident rules list 5-gallon and 20-gallon propane tanks and 16-oz propane cylinders.
The propane-specific ENV page says accepted tanks may be empty, full, or partially full.
If the container does not match the listed household sizes/types, contact ENV Disposal Branch rather than assuming acceptance.
prohibitions: Do not dispose of propane tanks in regular trash.

items.name: Tire

primary_pathway.next_action: When buying a new tire, use the dealer take-back requirement; otherwise, take eligible household tires to a City convenience center, Kapaʻa Transfer Station, or Kawailoa Transfer Station.

restrictions: Limit 4 tires per month at City disposal sites.
Passenger or light-truck tires only; no heavy-truck or equipment tires.
Tires may be with or without rims.
Keʻehi Transfer Station does not accept tires.

items.name: Motor oil

primary_pathway.next_action: Absorb the motor oil in an oil-change box or sealed plastic bag with absorbent material, then place it in regular refuse.

preparation: Use an oil-change box or absorb liquid in a plastic bag with shredded newspaper, old rags, sawdust, or similar absorbent material; seal before disposal.
restrictions: Do not use this rule for mixed oil/gas; ENV routes mixed oil/gas to a Household Hazardous Waste appointment.

items.name: Rock / dirt / concrete

primary_pathway.next_action: For household quantities, use Kapaʻa Transfer Station within its small-load limit or Waimānalo Gulch Sanitary Landfill (WGSL) within its resident load limit.

restrictions: Kapaʻa Transfer Station: up to five 5-gallon buckets of dirt/rock/sand/concrete/tile/asphalt/other non-combustible waste per day.
WGSL: up to two standard pickup-truck loads per day under the resident rules.
Large quantities/commercial vehicles can be redirected; residents should follow current site and vehicle rules.
notes: The general 'How to Dispose' page points to WGSL; the more specific resident-rules page additionally allows small quantities at Kapaʻa. V1 preserves both sources and applies the more specific rule.

items.name: Large metal item

primary_pathway.next_action: Schedule bulky-item collection or take the prepared metal item to a City disposal site and place it in the designated metal area.

preparation: If material can be disassembled/cut/broken down, keep it under 6 feet long and under 60 pounds.
Metal shelving: disassemble, bundle, and fasten.
Drain and properly dispose of fluids from lawn tools or small auto parts before metal disposal.
restrictions: Large automobile parts such as engines, transmissions, hoods, and doors are prohibited at resident City disposal sites.

items.name: Natural Christmas tree

primary_pathway.next_action: Remove decorations. Use the green-cart/manual-collection preparation that applies to your residence, or take the whole natural tree to an eligible listed drop-off location.

preparation: Do not flock the tree for green-waste/composting disposal.
Automated green cart: cut into lengths up to 3 feet and trim branches so the lid closes.
Manual collection: cut into lengths up to 3 feet and bundle.
restrictions: Whole natural-tree drop-off is listed at convenience centers except Wahiawā, Kapaʻa Transfer Station, and Hawaiian Earth Recycling.
Current holiday guidance says bulky appointments cannot be made for natural Christmas trees.
